string.text: Shows your own pictures instead of the game's. Put PNG or JPG files in the mod's Backgrounds folder: MainMenu for the main menu, Loading for the loading screens (and the few menus that reuse them). New files are picked up the next time the screen appears. Nothing changes while the folders are empty. Off, or the hotkey, brings back the game's own.

Which pictures the loading screens show, when there are pictures in the Backgrounds Loading folder. Mixed shows one of yours on about half the loading screens and one of the game's on the rest. Needs Use custom backgrounds to be on.
How a picture that is a different shape from the screen is fitted. Fill keeps it undistorted and crops the edges; Stretch shows all of it, squashed to the screen's shape.
Master switch. Off restores the vanilla look immediately.

Lists every UI brush and sprite the mod sees, and what it decided to treat it as, in Documents\Mount and Blade II Bannerlord\Logs\CustomisableUI.log. Useful if something is being recoloured that shouldn't be.
Keep colours added by other mods

Compatibility with mods that colour the interface to mean something, such as item rows tinted by quality. Panels, buttons and text that are already a clearly coloured shade (not black, white, grey or the game's usual browns) are left alone instead of being themed. A few of the game's own coloured buttons and panels stay as they are too.

Press to switch between your theme and the game's vanilla look, from anywhere (including this screen). Handy for comparing, and a way out if a combination makes the interface hard to read. Press again to bring your theme back.

Textured keeps the game's panel artwork and tints it. Flat replaces the artwork with a plain fill of exactly the colour below, so what you pick is what you get. Flat needs a panel colour: with 'Vanilla (no change)' the panels stay textured.

Tint for window and panel backgrounds. In the textured style the tint is multiplied with the original artwork, so pair darker colours with a higher brightness. In the flat style it is the colour itself.
Used when 'Custom (use hex code)' is picked above. Format: #RRGGBB, e.g. #2A3F8F.
0% keeps the vanilla colour, 100% applies the full tint.
1.00 is vanilla. Raise it if a dark tint makes panels too murky. With the flat style 1.00 is exactly your colour and the slider has a gentler effect.
Lower values let the game world show through panels. Keep it high enough to read text.

Flat style only. Panels that sit inside a window (popups, lists, rows) are drawn a step lighter, or darker for a pale colour, so they stand out from the window behind. 0% makes every panel exactly the same colour.

Flat style only. A thin, slightly darker edge around every flat panel, so neighbouring panels and list rows can be told apart. It shows most on lighter panel colours; on very dark ones the depth setting does more.
Tint for the decorative borders around panels.
Used when 'Custom (use hex code)' is picked above. Format: #RRGGBB.
Tint for button artwork (hover and pressed states keep their relative brightness).
Replaces the colour of all text. 'Auto' picks light or dark text to suit your panel and button colours.
0% keeps the vanilla colour, 100% replaces it completely.

If your text colour would be hard to read on your panel and button colours (pale text on a light panel, dark text on a dark one), light or dark text is used instead. Also corrects vanilla text when a theme makes it hard to read.
How much contrast 'Keep text readable' insists on, as a WCAG contrast ratio. 4.5:1 is the accessibility standard (AA) for normal text; 7:1 (AAA) is the enhanced level for low vision.

Losses, gains and warnings are drawn in red and green, which people with red-green colour blindness often can't tell apart. 'Colour-blind safe' swaps them for orange and blue. Any colour picked below takes priority over this.
Gains, bonuses and positive values: green text, and the game's 'positive' and 'bonus' text and slider fills. 'Vanilla' leaves them alone.
Losses, penalties and negative values: red text, and the game's 'negative' and 'penalty' text and slider fills.
Text the game marks as a warning.
Colour of the crosshair lines in battle. 'Vanilla' keeps the game's own.
The game turns the crosshair red when the target is invalid. This is the colour used instead.
The marker that flashes when you hit something. Vanilla is white.
The marker that flashes on a kill, and the headshot marker. Vanilla is red.
Lower values make the crosshair and its markers more transparent. 100% is vanilla.
Colour of the outline added by 'Text outline thickness'.
Adds an outline to text to keep it readable on busy or recoloured backgrounds. 0% leaves each piece of text with its vanilla outline.
Adds a soft dark halo behind text, which helps names stay readable over a busy map. 0% leaves each piece of text with its vanilla shadow.
Colour of the shadow added by 'Text shadow'.
Replaces the font used for most interface text (vanilla: Fira Sans Extra Condensed). Only applies to Latin-alphabet languages.
Replaces the decorative serif font used for titles and many labels (vanilla: Galahad). Only applies to Latin-alphabet languages.
Scales labels and most single-line text. Long passages (conversations, encyclopedia) keep their vanilla size.
Rotates the hue of panels, frames and buttons, in degrees. Applied on top of the tints above.
Negative values drain colour, positive values intensify it.
Negative values darken, positive values lighten.
Off (default): only panels, frames and buttons are graded. On: every sprite is, including icons, banners and portraits' frames.
Colour for allies: your own faction and anyone allied with it. 'Vanilla' leaves the game's own colours alone, so pick a colour for each of ally, enemy and neutral to switch them on.
Colour for enemies: anyone at war with your faction, including bandits.
Colour for everyone who is neither an ally nor an enemy.
Colour settlement bars on the map
The coloured bar behind each castle, town and village name on the campaign map. The game draws these in dark green, dark red or black.
Colour parties and settlements on the map
Draws party and settlement names and troop counts on the campaign map in their relation colour instead of their faction's colour. Your own party keeps its colour. Turn off to keep faction colours.
The ally, enemy and neutral troop numbers shown when you hover over a party.
In battle: the markers over formations, siege engine markers, and friendly and enemy name text.
My pictures and the game's, mixed
The game's pictures only (none of mine)
Flat (a plain fill of the colour)
Auto (light or dark to suit panels)
Customisable UI: showing the vanilla look. Press the hotkey again to bring your theme back.
Customisable UI: your theme is back.
